extra.message: User input from request.GET['copyline'] is directly concatenated into an HTML string without escaping, then returned as text/html. This allows reflected cross-site scripting: an attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript by crafting a malicious copyline parameter.

User-controlled JSON from request.body is parsed and passed to workset.update(change_set), allowing an attacker to override any property in the workset dictionary including 'is_admin', 'role', and 'credit_limit'. This is a mass assignment / object property override vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: User input from request.GET['lane'] or request.POST['lane'] is passed directly to redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL with an external lane value (e.g., https://evil.com) to redirect users to a malicious site, enabling phishing attacks.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The request body and Authorization header (which may contain bearer tokens or API keys) are logged via logger.warning(). This inserts sensitive credentials and data into log files, which may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or stored insecurely.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: User input from request.GET['ref'] is used to construct a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") and write to it without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (e.g., ../../etc/cron.d/evil) to write files outside the intended directory. Additionally, sensitive data (SSN, credit card number) is accepted via GET parameters and persisted.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: MD5 is used to hash user-supplied input. MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks. It should not be used for any security-sensitive purpose such as integrity verification or password hashing.

The course_identity_ping_341 endpoint has no authentication check (no _wrk_gate call). Any unauthenticated user can access this endpoint and submit arbitrary handle and channel parameters, which are reflected in the response. This violates the authentication pattern used by all other ops endpoints.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded verifier values ("north": "4812", "south": "5930") are used as credentials for authentication. These cannot be rotated without code changes and are visible to anyone with source access, enabling unauthorized access.

The Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header is set to the value of the request's Origin header without validation, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to true. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint, effectively bypassing the same-origin policy.

Security headers are explicitly disabled: X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' (disabling browser XSS filter) and Content-Security-Policy is set to empty (removing CSP protections). This removes defense-in-depth protections against cross-site scripting and content injection attacks.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is passed directly into a Jinja2 Template constructor and rendered. This allows server-side template injection (SSTI), enabling arbitrary code execution on the server. An attacker can execute system commands via payloads like {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}.

User input from request.GET['name'] is used directly as a filename component (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and the request body is written to that file without any path sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal (e.g., name=../../tmp/evil) to write arbitrary content to any location on the filesystem writable by the application process.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The random module is used to generate security-relevant codes/tokens. random.choice() is not cryptographically secure and its output can be predicted. The secrets module should be used instead for any token or nonce generation.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: XML is parsed from user request body using lxml.etree.XMLParser with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This configuration allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, enabling an attacker to read arbitrary files from the server, perform server-side request forgery, or cause denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Authorization is determined by a user-controlled cookie (ops_badge) or header (x-ops-badge). If the value equals 'lead', elevated access with payroll and casework data is granted. Since clients control their own cookies and headers, any attacker can set ops_badge=lead to bypass this authorization check and access privileged data.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is directly concatenated into a shell command string and executed via os.system(): "ping -c 1 " + host. This allows arbitrary command injection; an attacker can supply host=127.0.0.1;cat /etc/passwd to execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the application process.

SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context() when making an outbound HTTPS request. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks where an attacker could intercept or modify the communication, potentially exfiltrating sensitive data or injecting malicious responses.

The X-Forwarded-For header is trusted without validation to determine the client IP address (used in audit logs). Any client can spoof this header by setting X-Forwarded-For to an arbitrary value, allowing attackers to falsify IP addresses in audit log entries and cover their tracks.

The Django SECRET_KEY defaults to the hardcoded value 'local-dev-insecure-change-me' if the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. This key is used for cryptographic signing of sessions, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens. An attacker who knows this key can forge sessions, bypass CSRF protection, and generate valid password reset tokens.

DEBUG defaults to True when the DJANGO_DEBUG environment variable is not set. Running Django with DEBUG=True in production exposes sensitive information including detailed error tracebacks, database queries, settings values, and stack traces to anyone who triggers an error.

A hardcoded API key ('lms_demo_admin_api_key_for_local_checks') and shared password ('DemoPass123!') are defined in source code and used to seed the database. If this seed command is run in any environment, these credentials become active and anyone with access to the source code can authenticate as an admin.
